Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a
bounded polyhedral open set with a matching shape-regular affine simplicial
mesh family $\{\mathcal T_h\}$, and set $h:=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K\le1$.
Fix an integer $r\ge1$. On the reference simplex let
$(\widehat S_d,\widehat P,\widehat\Sigma)$ be an unisolvent real scalar
finite element whose finite-dimensional local space $\widehat P$ consists of
polynomials and contains $\mathbb P_r$. Assume each
degree of freedom has a bounded linear extension to
$W^{r+1,2}(\widehat S_d)$, and let $\widehat I$ be its interpolant. Suppose
there is a global map $I_h$ whose restriction to each cell is the affine
pullback of $\widehat I$, and that $I_hu\in V_h$ for the conforming discrete
space $V_h\subset H^1_0(\Omega)$ whenever
$u\in W^{r+1,2}(\Omega)\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$, where $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is the
closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ in $W^{1,2}(\Omega)$
([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]). Then a constant $C$ independent of
$h$ and $u$ satisfies
$$\|u-I_hu\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C h^r|u|_{W^{r+1,2}(\Omega)}.$$
The global conformity and zero-boundary mapping property of $I_h$ are explicit
hypotheses; this estimate does not assert them for arbitrary degrees of
freedom.

Assume the hypotheses of the stochastic Galerkin theorem with
$D\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, and suppose the
exact solution has the exact finite expansion
$$u(y)=\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}u_\alpha\psi_\alpha(y),\qquad u_\alpha\in H^r(D)\cap H_0^1(D),$$
for integers $k\ge0$ and $1\le\ell\le r\le k+1$. Choose a fixed
reference finite element whose polynomial space contains $\mathbb P_k$ and
whose unisolvent degrees of freedom are bounded on $W^{\ell,2}$ of the
reference cell; let its reference interpolant reproduce $\mathbb P_k$ and
define local interpolants by affine pullback as in
[[thm-local-finite-element-interpolation-estimates]]. Let
$\{\mathcal T_h\}$ be a shape-regular family of matching affine simplicial
meshes as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], with maximum cell
diameter $h$, and assume for each mesh that a globally conforming spatial
interpolant $I_h$ maps these coefficients into its finite-element space,
restricts cellwise to those local interpolants, and preserves the zero boundary
condition. These are the generic bounded-degree-of-freedom hypotheses of the
local estimate. Then for the stochastic Galerkin solution
$U_{\Lambda,h}$,
$$\|u-U_{\Lambda,h}\|_{L^2_\rho(H_0^1(D))} \le \frac{a^*}{a_*}\,C h^{r-1} \left(\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda}|u_\alpha|_{H^r(D)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
The regularity and finite-expansion assumptions are explicit; this is not a
general spatial rate for arbitrary random solutions.

current_use.excerpt: A compatible labeled initial mesh is a finite matching affine simplicial triangulation $\mathcal T_0$ of a polygon in $\mathbb R^2$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], equipped with labels on its edges such that each triangle has one edge labeled $0$ and two labeled $1$, and every shared edge has the same label from both incident triangles. Matching means that distinct cell interiors are disjoint and any nonempty cell intersection is a whole common face: in two dimensions it may be a vertex or an edge. For a descendant triangle of generation $g(K)$, its three edge labels, in any order, are $(g(K)+1,g(K)+1,g(K))$. The unique edge labeled $g(K)$ is its reference edge.

current_use.excerpt:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a matching affine simplicial mesh of $\Omega$ as defined
in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. Fix $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and an integer $q\ge1$. On each
cell let $\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb K^q)$ denote the
restrictions to $K$ of $\mathbb K^q$-valued polynomials of total degree at
most $k$. The **broken polynomial space** is the finite product
$$V_h^{\mathrm{br}}:=\prod_{K\in\mathcal T}\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb K^q),$$
viewed as functions defined almost everywhere cell by cell. For an interior
facet $F=K\cap K'$, the **jump** is the difference of the two polynomial
traces, with either fixed ordering of $K,K'$; its vanishing is independent of
that ordering. The **conforming polynomial space** is
$$V_h^{\mathrm{conf}}:=\{v\in V_h^{\mathrm{br}}:v|_{F,K}=v|_{F,K'}\text{ on every interior facet }F\}.$$
The **zero-boundary subspace** consists of those $v\in V_h^{\mathrm{conf}}$
whose polynomial trace is zero on every boundary facet. These are algebraic
definitions. The Sobolev inclusions and the zero-boundary closure conclusion
are proved separately in the corresponding local theorems on matching
piecewise polynomials and zero-boundary values. If $\mathcal T=\varnothing$,
then $\Omega=\varnothing$ by the mesh definition; the empty product is the
zero vector space consisting of the unique empty function, and the trace
conditions are vacuous.

current_use.excerpt:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral
domain with a finite matching affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T$. Here
Lipschitz polyhedral means that the boundary is a finite union of flat
simplex faces and, near each boundary point after a rigid coordinate change,
$\Omega$ lies on one side of a Lipschitz graph. Let $\mathcal F^\circ$ and
$\mathcal F^\partial$ be its interior and boundary facets. For a cellwise
affine function $v$, write $v_K$ for its polynomial restriction to $K$. The
broken gradient $\nabla_hv$ is defined by $(\nabla_hv)|_K:=\nabla v_K$.
For a facet $F$ and an integrable function $w$ on $F$, let $h_F:=\operatorname{diam}(F)$ and write $\operatorname{avg}_F(w):=|F|^{-1}\int_Fw\,dS$.
The homogeneous Crouzeix–Raviart space is
$$V_h^{CR,0}:=\left\{v\in L^2(\Omega): v_K\in\mathbb P_1(K)\ \text{for each }K\in\mathcal T,\quad \int_F(v_{K^+}-v_{K^-})\,dS=0\ \text{for }F=K^+\cap K^-\in\mathcal F^\circ,\quad \int_Fv_K\,dS=0\ \text{for }F\in\mathcal F^\partial\right\}.$$
The ordering $K^+,K^-$ on an interior facet is arbitrary; the zero-mean
condition is independent of that ordering. The functions need not agree
pointwise on a facet and need not belong to $H^1(\Omega)$.

Let $d\ge2$ and let $K$ be a nondegenerate affine $d$-simplex with vertices
$a_0,\ldots,a_d$ and facets $F_i$ opposite $a_i$. Write
$\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$ for its barycentric coordinate functions, so
$\lambda_i(a_j)=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. The local
Crouzeix–Raviart polynomial space is $\mathbb P_1(K)$, the real affine
functions on $K$. Its face-average functionals are
$$\sigma_{K,F_i}(p):=\frac1{|F_i|}\int_{F_i}p\,dS,\qquad p\in\mathbb P_1(K).$$
The candidate dual shape polynomial associated with $F_i$ is
$$\phi_{K,F_i}:=1-d\lambda_i.$$
The next item proves that these $d+1$ functionals are unisolvent and that the
displayed polynomials form their dual basis. No pointwise continuity across
different cells is part of this local element.

Let $d\ge2$ and let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of a bounded polyhedral open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ in the sense of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. A **degree map** is a function $p:\mathcal T\to\mathbb N_0$ with finite values. The broken simplex space associated with $(\mathcal T,p)$ is
$$
V^{\mathrm{br}}(\mathcal T,p):=\{v\in L^2(\Omega):v|_K\in\mathbb P_{p_K}(K)\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T\},
$$
where $p_K:=p(K)$ and $\mathbb P_m(K)$ denotes restrictions of real polynomials of total degree at most $m$. Its **conforming hp space** is the subspace of functions whose two polynomial traces agree on every interior facet. The zero-boundary hp space further requires the polynomial trace to vanish on every boundary facet. For an interior facet $F=K\cap K'$, its trace degree is $p_F:=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; equality of the two traces means that their common polynomial belongs to $\mathbb P_{p_F}(F)$.

Choose one orientation for every mesh edge and face and the ambient orientation for each tetrahedron, with incidence signs given by [[def-oriented-simplicial-cell-chains]]. Write $t_e$ for the unit tangent in the chosen direction of an edge $e$, and $n_F$ for the unit normal determined by the chosen orientation of a face $F$ and the ambient orientation. On a tetrahedron $K$ with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3$, list the vertices in any order and let $P_1(K)$ denote scalar polynomials of total degree at most one. For an ordered edge $[i,j]$, put $\phi_{ij}=\lambda_i\nabla\lambda_j-\lambda_j\nabla\lambda_i$; reversing its orientation changes the sign. Set
$$W_h^0:=\{q\in C^0(\overline\Omega):q|_K\in P_1(K)\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T\}.$$
The first-family lowest-order Nedelec space is
$$N_h^1:=\{u\in H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega):u|_K\in\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{ij}:0\le i<j\le3\}\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T,\text{ and every global edge }e\text{ has one common oriented circulation }\int_e u|_K\cdot t_e\,ds\text{ for all }K\supset e\}.$$
The local Raviart–Thomas space is $RT_0(K)=\{a+c x:a\in\mathbb R^3,\ c\in\mathbb R\}$. With $H(\operatorname{div};\Omega)$ as defined by [[def-na-hdiv-space]], set
$$N_h^2:=\{v\in H(\operatorname{div};\Omega):v|_K\in RT_0(K)\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T,\text{ and every global face }F\text{ has one common oriented flux }\int_F v|_K\cdot n_F\,dS\text{ for all }K\supset F\},\qquad N_h^3:=\{q\in L^2(\Omega):q|_K\text{ is constant for every }K\in\mathcal T\}.$$

its standard triangular-grid subdivision, obtained by dividing each side into
$n$ equal segments and drawing the parallel grid lines, consists of equilateral
cells of side $1/n$; these cells form a shape-regular family with
$h/\rho=2\sqrt3$.

translates and reflections of the triangle with vertices
$(0,0),(1,0),(0,\epsilon)$; their $h/\rho\to\infty$, so this mesh family
is not shape regular under the convention of
[[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]].

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F(\widehat x)=A\widehat x+b$ be an affine bijection from a bounded open
set $\widehat K\subset\mathbb R^d$ to $K$, where $A$ is invertible, and let
$1\le p\le\infty$. For every integer $r\ge0$ and scalar
$v\in W^{r,p}(K)$, the pullback $\widehat v:=v\circ F$ belongs to
$W^{r,p}(\widehat K)$. For $r\ge1$ its first weak derivatives satisfy
$$D_{\widehat x_j}\widehat v=\sum_{i=1}^d A_{ij}(D_{x_i}v)\circ F,$$
and higher derivatives are obtained by applying this constant-matrix rule
repeatedly. In particular, for each $0\le m\le r$,
$$|\widehat v|_{W^{m,p}(\widehat K)}\le C(d,m)\|A\|^m|\det A|^{-1/p}|v|_{W^{m,p}(K)},$$
where $|\det A|^{-1/p}:=1$ for $p=\infty$. The reverse estimate holds
with $A^{-1}$ and $|\det A|^{1/p}$ in place of $A$ and
$|\det A|^{-1/p}$.

$F\subset\partial K$ a facet, and $1/2<r\le1$. Every $q\in H^r(K)$ has a
single-valued $L^2(F)$ trace $\gamma_Fq$. For $1/2<r<1$,
$$\|\gamma_Fq\|_{L^2(F)} \le C\left(h_K^{-1/2}\|q\|_{L^2(K)} +h_K^{r-1/2}[q]_{H^r(K)}\right),$$
and
$$\|\gamma_Fq-\operatorname{avg}_F\gamma_Fq\|_{L^2(F)} \le C h_K^{r-1/2}[q]_{H^r(K)},$$
while for $r=1$,
$$\|\gamma_Fq\|_{L^2(F)} \le C\left(h_K^{-1/2}\|q\|_{L^2(K)} +h_K^{1/2}\|\nabla q\|_{L^2(K)}\right),$$
and the face-mean fluctuation is bounded by
$C h_K^{1/2}\|\nabla q\|_{L^2(K)}$.
The constant depends only on $d$, the shape-regularity bound, and $r$.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded Lipschitz polyhedron with a matching shape-regular affine tetrahedral mesh $\mathcal T_h$. There are a positive continuous piecewise affine function $g_h$, a smooth bounded vector field $b$ on a neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$, and positive constants $c,C,r,\epsilon_0$, independent of the mesh, with the following properties. On $K$, $c h_K\le g_h\le C h_K$ and $\operatorname{Lip}(g_h)\le C$, where $h_K=\operatorname{diam}K$. Put
$$F_{t,y}^{\pm}(x)=x+t g_h(x)(\pm b(x)+r y),\qquad |y|\le1,\quad 0<t\le\epsilon_0.$$
The maps are uniformly bi-Lipschitz on their domain. For the plus sign, $F_{t,y}^{+}(\overline\Omega)\subset\Omega$. For the minus sign, $F_{t,y}^{-}(\partial\Omega)\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline\Omega$, at distance at least $ctg_h(x)$ from $\partial\Omega$. The same interior distance lower bound holds for the plus sign at boundary points. The images of $K$ and all homotopies $s\mapsto F_{st,y}^{\pm}(x)$, $x\in K$, lie within distance $Ct h_K$ of $K$. Their intersections with $\Omega$ are contained in a vertex patch $\omega_K$ of uniformly bounded overlap, after decreasing $\epsilon_0$ if necessary. All constants may depend on $\Omega$ and the shape-regularity bound. No ratio of global maximum to minimum mesh size occurs.

For $u\in H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$, the formula
$$\langle\gamma_\tau u,[v]\rangle:=\int_\Omega(\operatorname{curl}u\cdot v-u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v)\,dx$$
defines a bounded linear functional on $T(\partial\Omega)$, independent of the representative $v$. For smooth $u$ and smooth $v$ it equals $\int_{\partial\Omega}(n\times u)\cdot v\,dS$. Let $h:=\max_Kh_K$, $\ell_\Omega:=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega)$, and $1/2<s\le1$. For every $\zeta\in H^{1+s}(\Omega)$, with no boundary-value or PDE assumption,
$$\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n\zeta\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C h^{1/2}\|\zeta\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)}=C_T h^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2}\|\zeta\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)},\qquad C_T:=C\ell_\Omega^{-1/2}.$$
The trace is the restriction of the whole-space Fourier hyperplane trace and agrees with the facet trace in [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]]. The constant $C_T$ may depend on the fixed domain, $d$, $s$, and the Fourier normalization, but not on the mesh.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix $d\ge2$, $1/2<s\le1$, and a shape-regular affine simplicial mesh family as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. For $0<s<1$ and a scalar or vector-valued function $w$ on a cell $K$, define
$$|w|_{s,K}^2:=\int_K\int_K\frac{|w(x)-w(y)|^2}{|x-y|^{d+2s}}\,dx\,dy;$$
for $s=1$ set $|w|_{1,K}:=\|\nabla w\|_{L^2(K)}$ (componentwise for vectors). For every cell $K$, facet $F\subset\partial K$, and $w\in H^s(K)$ in the restriction convention of [[def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential-sobolev-spaces]], the trace from [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]] satisfies
$$\|T_Fw\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C\bigl(h_K^{-1}\|w\|_{L^2(K)}^2+h_K^{2s-1}|w|_{s,K}^2\bigr).$$
For $0<s<1$, the norm $\bigl(\|w\|_{L^2(K)}^2+|w|_{s,K}^2\bigr)^{1/2}$ is equivalent on a fixed reference simplex to the restriction $H^s$ norm. At $s=1$ the displayed estimate is the weak $H^1$ trace inequality; no additional identification of the full intrinsic weak-$H^1$ space with a restriction space is asserted. Constants are uniform over the shape-regular family and depend only on $d,s$ and its shape bound.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $E$ be a bounded polyhedral open control domain and let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of $E$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. Let $U_h\subset L^2(E)$ be the subspace of functions constant on each cell. Let the bounds $q_a,q_b$ in [[def-pde-box-control-set]] be constant on each cell and satisfy $q_a\le q_b$. Put $Q_h=U_h\cap Q_{ad}(q_a,q_b)$. For $r\in L^2(E)$ define
$$
(P_{Q_h}r)|_K=\operatorname{clip}_{[q_a|_K,q_b|_K]}\left(\frac1{|K|}\int_Kr(x)\,dx\right),\qquad K\in\mathcal T_h,
$$
where $\operatorname{clip}_{[a,b]}(s)=\min\{b,\max\{a,s\}\}$. Then $P_{Q_h}r$ is the unique $L^2(E)$-nearest point in $Q_h$ to $r$, and $P_{Q_h}$ is nonexpansive: $\|P_{Q_h}r-P_{Q_h}s\|_{L^2(E)}\le\|r-s\|_{L^2(E)}$.

Let $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded polyhedral open control domain, and let $\{\mathcal T_h\}$ be a family of matching affine simplicial meshes of $E$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. $$
(\Pi_hq)|_K=|K|^{-1}\int_Kq.
$$

\|q-\Pi_hq\|_{L^2(E)}\le C h\,|q|_{H^1(E)},

Let $\widehat K$ be the reference simplex of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], let $\alpha=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_d)$ have nonnegative real entries, and let $\omega_\alpha=\prod_{j=0}^d\lambda_j^{\alpha_j}$, where $\lambda_j$ are its barycentric coordinates. Give polynomials the inner product $\langle f,g\rangle_\alpha=\int_{\widehat K}\omega_\alpha fg$. Put $\mathbb P_{-1}=\{0\}$ and let $E_n=\mathbb P_n(\widehat K)\ominus\mathbb P_{n-1}(\widehat K)$ in this weighted inner product. For a finite sum $u=\sum_{n\ge0}u_n$, $u_n\in E_n$, define
$$
\|u\|_{\mathcal H_\alpha^s}^2:=\sum_{n\ge0}(1+\mu_n)^s\|u_n\|_{L^2(\omega_\alpha)}^2,\qquad \mu_n=n(n+d+|\alpha|),
$$
and define $\mathcal H_\alpha^s$ as the completion of these finite sums. If $m\ge\ell\ge0$, its orthogonal degree truncation $P_pu=\sum_{n=0}^pu_n$ obeys
$$
\|u-P_pu\|_{\mathcal H_\alpha^\ell}\le(1+\mu_{p+1})^{-(m-\ell)/2}\|u\|_{\mathcal H_\alpha^m}.
$$
For $q\in\mathbb P_p(\widehat K)$, $\|q\|_{\mathcal H_\alpha^m}\le(1+\mu_p)^{(m-\ell)/2}\|q\|_{\mathcal H_\alpha^\ell}$. These are estimates in the explicitly coefficient-defined scale $\mathcal H_\alpha^s$; they do not identify that scale with ordinary unweighted $H^s(\widehat K)$.

whose polynomial space contains $\mathbb P_k$. Assume its degrees of
freedom are bounded on $W^{\ell,p}(\widehat S_d)$ for an integer
$\ell\ge1$, let $r,m\in\mathbb N_0$, and let $\widehat I$ be its
interpolant. Thus
$\widehat Iq=q$ for $q\in\mathbb P_k$. On a shape-regular affine mesh
as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], for each cell $K$ with its
orientation-preserving reference map $F_K$ define
$$I_Kv=(\widehat I(v\circ F_K))\circ F_K^{-1}.$$

Assume Countable Choice and the elliptic control problem of [[def-linear-elliptic-pde-constrained-control-problem]] on a shape-regular affine simplicial mesh family, with cellwise-constant box bounds and P1 conforming state and adjoint spaces. Let $U_h\subset U$ be the cellwise-constant control space and $Q_h=U_h\cap Q_{ad}$. For each $q\in U$, let $u_h(q)\in V_h$ be the chosen affine finite-element state map, and define the finite-element reduced objective on $U$ by
$$
\widehat J_h(q)=\frac12\|Ju_h(q)-u_d\|_H^2+\frac\alpha2\|q\|_U^2.
$$
Let $p_h(q)\in V_h$ be its associated discrete adjoint. Require adjoint consistency for this same state map and objective, namely
$$
D\widehat J_h(q)[r]=(B^*p_h(q)+\alpha q,r)_U\qquad(q,r\in U).
$$
Write $g_h(q)=B^*p_h(q)+\alpha q$ and $g(q)=\nabla\widehat J(q)$. Let $q_*$ be the continuous minimizer and $q_h$ the minimizer of $\widehat J_h$ over $Q_h$. Assume $q_*\in H^1(E)$, the projected adjoints satisfy $\|B^*p_h(q_h)\|_{H^1(E)}\le C_p$ uniformly in $h$, and the exact state/adjoint finite-element gradient error obeys
$$
\sup_{q\in Q_h}\|g_h(q)-g(q)\|_U\le C_g h.
$$
The last bound is supplied by [[lem-fem-control-gradient-residual-bound]] when its state and adjoint approximations are the same $u_h$ and $p_h$ used in $\widehat J_h$ and the stated primal/adjoint P1 approximation errors and every Strang form/load defect are $O(h)$ uniformly over $Q_h$. Then there is a constant $C$ independent of $h$ such that
$$
\|q_h-q_*\|_{L^2(E)}\le C h.
$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded
polyhedral open set, let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine
simplicial mesh of $\Omega$, and choose $k\in\mathbb N_0$. Let
$V=W^{1,2}_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with its $W^{1,2}$ norm,
$H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and let $V^*$ be the continuous dual of $V$;
these spaces form the separable real evolution triple proved in
[[lem-parabolic-zero-boundary-sobolev-space-is-separable]]. Let $V_h$ be the
scalar degree-at-most-$k$ conforming polynomial subspace on $\mathcal T_h$
whose polynomial traces vanish on every boundary facet, as defined by
[[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]. Suppose the real bilinear
form $a(t;\cdot,\cdot)$ on $V$ is scalar measurable and there is one null
set outside which it is bounded by $M$ and coercive by $\alpha>0$ on $V$.
Let $f\in L^2(0,T;V^*)$ and $u_h^0\in V_h$. Then there is a unique
$u_h\in H^1(0,T;V_h)$ with $u_h(0)=u_h^0$ satisfying
$$((u_h)'(t),v_h)_H+a(t;u_h(t),v_h)=\langle f(t),v_h\rangle_{V^*,V} \qquad(v_h\in V_h)$$
for almost every $t$. For every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\|u_h(t)\|_H^2+\alpha\int_0^t\|u_h(s)\|_V^2\,ds \le\|u_h^0\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\int_0^t\|f(s)\|_{V^*}^2\,ds.$$

Let $d\ge1$. If $d=1$, let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite oriented interval mesh of $\Omega=(a,b)$, $a<b$, from [[def-pe04-one-dimensional-interval-mesh-and-broken-polynomials]]; if $d\ge2$, let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of $\Omega$. Let $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$ be constant, and let $u_h$ solve [[def-pe04-upwind-dg-transport-discretization]] with inflow data $g$. Assume Countable Choice when $d\ge2$, as required by the affine-simplex Green supplier; no choice assumption is needed for the interval branch. Write $\Gamma_+=\{x\in\partial\Omega:\beta\cdot n>0\}$ and $\Gamma_- =\{x\in\partial\Omega:\beta\cdot n<0\}$. For an interior facet $F=K^-\cap K^+$ choose a unit normal $n_F$ from $K^-$ to $K^+$ and write $[u_h]=u_h^+-u_h^-$. In dimension one, integrals over facets and boundary points mean sums with respect to zero-dimensional surface measure. Then
$$\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\|u_h\|_{L^2(K)}^2+\frac12\sum_{F\text{ interior}}\int_F|\beta\cdot n_F|[u_h]^2\,dS+\frac12\int_{\Gamma_+}(\beta\cdot n)u_h^2\,dS+\frac12\int_{\Gamma_-}|\beta\cdot n|(u_h-g)^2\,dS=\frac12\int_{\Gamma_-}|\beta\cdot n|g^2\,dS.$$
In particular, zero inflow data give a nonincreasing semidiscrete $L^2$ norm. This result is semidiscrete and makes no claim about a time integrator.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded contractible Lipschitz
polyhedral cavity with connected boundary. Let $\epsilon,\mu>0$ be constant
scalar coefficients and let $\{\mathcal T_{h_n}\}_{n\ge1}$ be a
shape-regular refining family of matching affine tetrahedral meshes, with
$h_n\to0$. Use the full continuous and discrete curl-kernel quotient gauges
$X$ and $X_{h_n}$ of
[[def-na-pe11-maxwell-cavity-eigenproblem]]. Suppose the three PE09
supplier statements on regular decomposition,
[[thm-na-discrete-compactness-and-poincare-lowest-order-nedelec]], and
[[thm-na-uniformly-bounded-commuting-cochain-projection]] hold for this exact
domain, boundary convention and mesh family. Then the continuous PEC curl-curl
problem has isolated positive eigenvalues of finite multiplicity. For every
isolated continuous eigenvalue $\lambda>0$ of multiplicity $m$, choose
$\delta>0$ so that $I=(\lambda-\delta,\lambda+\delta)$ has
$\lambda-\delta>0$ and its closure contains no other continuous eigenvalue.
Then $I$ contains exactly $m$ discrete eigenvalues for all sufficiently large
$n$; these converge to $\lambda$ and their eigenspaces converge to the
continuous eigenspace in symmetric $L^2$ gap. If positive discrete eigenvalues converge to a finite
limit, that limit is a continuous eigenvalue. Thus the method has no nonzero
spectral pollution. No claim selects convergent individual eigenvectors
inside a repeated eigenspace.

For every macro cell $K$ in [[alg-fehmm-periodic-cell-micro-macro]], the coefficient $b_K$ satisfies $\lambda\le b_K\le\Lambda$. For each $p\in\mathbb R^2$, both the full cell problem on $V_\#$ and its restriction to $W_{\mathcal M}$ have unique solutions $w_{K,p}$ and $w^h_{K,p}$. The tensors
$$A_K^{\rm ex}p=\int_Yb_K(p+\nabla w_{K,p}),\qquad A_K^hp=\int_Yb_K(p+\nabla w^h_{K,p})$$
are symmetric and satisfy $\lambda I\le A_K^{\rm ex},A_K^h\le\Lambda I$. Consequently the macro FE-HMM system in the algorithm has a unique solution. The exact Gaussian-elimination calls specified there terminate without the `singular-system` branch and return the unique solutions of the assembled micro and macro variational systems.

current_use.excerpt:
Assume Countable Choice. Assume the real scalar finite-element setting of
[[cor-shape-regular-affine-fe-primal-energy-approximation]], and set
$V:=H^1_0(\Omega)$ with its usual $H^1$ norm. Let $V_h\subseteq V$ be the
stated conforming discrete space, let $a:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ be the same
bounded coercive form as in
[[thm-cea-quasi-optimality-for-conforming-galerkin-approximations]], and let
$u\in W^{r+1,2}(\Omega)\cap V$ and $u_h\in V_h$ solve the continuous and
discrete equations for the same bounded linear datum $F:V\to\mathbb R$;
assume also that $V_h$ is finite-dimensional. The natural inclusion
$J:V\to L^2(\Omega)$ obeys $\|Jv\|_{L^2}\le\|v\|_{H^1}$. For
$e:=J(u-u_h)$, let $z_e$ be the adjoint solution from
[[thm-aubin-nitsche-l2-error-estimate-under-adjoint-regularity]]. Suppose
there are $s\in(0,1]$, a normed regularity space $R_s\subseteq V$ for $z_e$,
and constants $C_D,C_R$ independent of $h$ and $e$ such that
$$\|z_e\|_{R_s}\le C_R\|e\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$
$$\inf_{w_h\in V_h}\|z_e-w_h\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C_D h^s\|z_e\|_{R_s}.$$
Then
$$\|u-u_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le \frac{M^2}{\alpha}C_{\rm FE}C_DC_R h^{r+s}|u|_{W^{r+1,2}(\Omega)}.$$
Here $C_{\rm FE}$ is the primal interpolation constant and $M,\alpha$ are
the boundedness and coercivity constants of $a$. In a full-adjoint Poisson
branch, one may take $R_1=H^2(\Omega)\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$ with the $H^2$ norm,
provided both displayed dual bounds hold. The $h^{r+1}$ rate is conditional
on those bounds and the primal approximation bound; no full-adjoint
regularity is asserted on an arbitrary Lipschitz domain.

current_use.excerpt:
Assume Countable Choice and the real scalar finite-element setting of
[[cor-shape-regular-affine-fe-primal-energy-approximation]], on a
shape-regular affine mesh family with $h\le1$. Let $V=H^1_0(\Omega)$
with its $H^1$ norm,
$H=L^2(\Omega)$, and let $a$ be a time-independent bounded coercive form
with constants $M,\alpha$. Let $R_h$ be its Ritz projection and let $u_h$
be the semidiscrete solution initialized by $u_h(0)=R_hu(0)$. Assume the
continuous solution obeys $u\in H^1(0,T;V)$,
$$u\in L^\infty(0,T;W^{r+1,2}(\Omega)\cap V),\qquad u'\in L^2(0,T;W^{r+1,2}(\Omega)\cap V),$$
for an integer $r\ge1$. For almost every $t$, assume the adjoint solution
and approximation inequalities in
[[cor-aubin-nitsche-h-r-plus-s-rate-under-primal-and-dual-approximation]]
hold for each target $w=u(t)$ and $w=u'(t)$ with common
$s\in(0,1]$, $C_D$, and $C_R$, uniformly in $h,t$. Let $C_{\rm FE}$ be the
primal interpolation constant in that corollary and put
$$C_A=\frac{M^2}{\alpha}C_{\rm FE}C_DC_R, \qquad c_i=\|V\hookrightarrow H\|.$$
Then $\rho=R_hu-u$ and $\theta=u_h-R_hu$ satisfy
$$\|\rho\|_{L^\infty(0,T;V)} \le\frac M\alpha C_{\rm FE}h^r \|u\|_{L^\infty(0,T;W^{r+1,2})},$$
$$\|\rho\|_{L^\infty(0,T;H)} \le C_Ah^{r+s}\|u\|_{L^\infty(0,T;W^{r+1,2})},\qquad \|\rho'\|_{L^2(0,T;H)} \le C_Ah^{r+s}\|u'\|_{L^2(0,T;W^{r+1,2})},$$
and
$$\|\theta\|_{L^\infty(0,T;H)} \le\frac{c_i C_A}{\sqrt\alpha}h^{r+s} \|u'\|_{L^2(0,T;W^{r+1,2})},\qquad \|\theta\|_{L^2(0,T;V)} \le\frac{c_i C_A}{\alpha}h^{r+s} \|u'\|_{L^2(0,T;W^{r+1,2})}.$$
Consequently, $\|u_h-u\|_{L^\infty(0,T;H)}$ is bounded by the sum of the two
$L^\infty(0,T;H)$ bounds for $\rho,\theta$, and
$$\|u_h-u\|_{L^2(0,T;V)} \le\sqrt T\frac M\alpha C_{\rm FE}h^r \|u\|_{L^\infty(0,T;W^{r+1,2})} +\frac{c_i C_A}{\alpha}h^{r+s} \|u'\|_{L^2(0,T;W^{r+1,2})}.$$
In particular, the full-adjoint branch $s=1$ gives the conditional
semidiscrete max-in-time rate $h^{r+1}$ in $L^\infty(H)$; it requires both stated dual hypotheses and
does not assert full adjoint regularity on an arbitrary polyhedral domain.

current_use.excerpt: Input the exact dyadic square $[-1,1]^2$, a tolerance $0<\tau\le1/4$, and the exact shear $\Phi(x,y)=(x,y+x^2/4)$. Use the unweighted indexed corner list $S=((1,(-1,-1)),(2,(1,-1)),(3,(1,1)),(4,(-1,1)))$ with all weights absent, and call [[alg-incremental-planar-delaunay-edge-flips]] in its ordinary $g=0$ branch with no prescribed insertion permutation, so sites are inserted in increasing identifier order. If the call does not return a triangulation, return unresolved. Verify that the output consists of two triangles covering the square and sharing one diagonal; otherwise return unresolved. The boundary features are the four closed edges and four vertices; features are incident when their sets intersect, and separation is the minimum Euclidean distance between nonincident feature sets. Record the interior boundary-angle certificate $\alpha=\pi/2$ and the nonincident-feature separation certificate $\sigma=1$. Label the shared diagonal reference on both triangles and label the boundary edges nonreference. For each seed triangle, sort its three input site identifiers increasingly and use the resulting triple as its seed key. Sort the two distinct keys lexicographically and assign operational root ranks $1,2$ in that order. Initialize their identifiers $(1,\varnothing),(2,\varnothing)$ and stored vertex lists by [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]], retaining the just-assigned compatible reference-edge labels. All subsequent calls use the resulting persistent root-and-binary-path order, including on generated children; the site-key order is bookkeeping and does not relabel an edge. Set $k=0$. While $(3/2)2^{-k}(2\sqrt2)>\tau$, set $\eta_K^2=1$, $o_K^2=0$ on every current cell and call [[alg-dorfler-marking-and-conforming-nvb-refinement]] with $\theta_E=1$, $\theta_O=1$. Start the cycle budget at $B=1$; if the call returns `budget-exhausted`, retry from the unchanged mesh with $B$ doubled until it returns `complete`. A complete call requests three generations on every cell and uses recursive conformity closure; then set $k\leftarrow k+1$ and test the diameter bound again. Map every output reference triangle by the common shear $\Phi$ and return the mapped cells, feature certificates, and $k$. If a predicate is unresolved, the Delaunay seed does not have the stated two-triangle form, or closure returns invalid input, return `unresolved`.

current_use.excerpt: Input: a finite labeled conforming mesh $\mathcal T$, exact nonnegative arrays $(\eta_K^2)_{K\in\mathcal T}$ and $(o_K^2)_{K\in\mathcal T}$, where $\eta_K^2$ is the cell estimator contribution and $o_K^2$ the cell data-oscillation contribution, bulk-fraction parameters $\theta_E,\theta_O\in(0,1]$, a per-call total bisection budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$, and a stable total order of mesh identifiers. On the first call on a mesh not yet carrying operational forest identifiers, rank its cells by the supplied order and initialize the operational roots and vertex lists of [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]]. This initialization preserves the supplied order on those cells and does not change their geometric generations or labels. On subsequent calls retain that forest decoration and use its identifier order. Thus each current input leaf, including every generated descendant, has a specified identifier. For an array $q_K\ge0$ and $\theta\in(0,1]$, sort by decreasing $q_K$ and then increasing identifier. If $\sum_Kq_K=0$, return the empty set. Otherwise return the shortest initial segment whose sum is at least $\theta\sum_Kq_K$. Thus these parameters are fractions of the squared contributions (the square-root convention for the usual estimator-norm parameter). Call the resulting sets $M_E,M_O$ and set $M=M_E\cup M_O$.

current_use.excerpt:
Fix a compatible initial triangulation $\mathcal T_0$, its 2D NVB family $\mathbb T(\mathcal T_0)$ from [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]], and a weak solution $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ of the symmetric $A=I$, $b=0$ model in [[def-afem-p1-residual-estimator-and-data-oscillation]]. For a conforming refinement $\mathcal T$, let $V(\mathcal T)$ be its continuous P1 zero-boundary space and define
$$E(\mathcal T;u)=\inf_{v\in V(\mathcal T)}\|\nabla(u-v)\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad E_N(u)=\inf_{\substack{\mathcal T\in\mathbb T(\mathcal T_0)\\ \#\mathcal T-\#\mathcal T_0\le N}}E(\mathcal T;u).$$
For $s>0$, the approximation seminorm and class are
$$|u|_{\mathbb A_s}=\sup_{N\ge0}(N+1)^sE_N(u),\qquad \mathbb A_s=\{u\in H_0^1(\Omega):|u|_{\mathbb A_s}<\infty\}.$$
The infimum is over a nonempty finite-budget set because $\mathcal T_0$ is allowed. This definition concerns best energy approximation, not the number of cells selected by an algorithm. For the symmetric Laplace Galerkin solution, [[thm-cea-quasi-optimality-for-conforming-galerkin-approximations]] supplies the unique exact solution, while [[lem-galerkin-orthogonality-for-conforming-galerkin-approximations]] gives orthogonality in the gradient inner product. Expanding the square shows that the exact Galerkin error equals $E(\mathcal T;u)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice used by the weak Dirichlet Poisson existence supplier. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded polygon, $\mathcal T_0$ a compatible shape-regular 2D NVB mesh, and $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ solve $-\Delta u=f$ with $f$ piecewise constant on $\mathcal T_0$. Run the exact P1 algorithm with three-generation refinement; assume each per-call budget suffices for every refinement through iteration $k$. Write $U_k$ for the unique exact P1 Galerkin solution on $\mathcal T_k$, estimator bulk parameter $0<\theta_E\le\min(1,(1-\lambda^2)/(C_{\rm loc}C_{\rm eff}))$ for a fixed $0<\lambda<1$, as in [[lem-afem-dorfler-marking-cardinality]], and any fixed oscillation parameter $\theta_O\in(0,1]$. If $u\in\mathbb A_s$ from [[def-afem-p1-approximation-class]] for $0<s\le\frac12$, then
$$\|\nabla(u-U_k)\|_2\le C|u|_{\mathbb A_s}(1+\#\mathcal T_k-\#\mathcal T_0)^{-s},$$
where $C$ depends on the initial mesh, marking parameters and estimator constants. This is an optimal-complexity theorem only for the Laplacian and P0 initial data.

current_use.excerpt:
Let $(V,H,V^*)$ be a real evolution triple and let $V_h\subset V$ be a
finite-dimensional conforming subspace. In a mesh instance, the algebraic
piecewise-polynomial conventions are those of
[[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]; the required inclusion into
$V$ is an explicit hypothesis of this definition. Let
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ be time-independent,
bounded, and coercive as in
[[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]], with constants
$M$ and $\alpha>0$. For $u\in V$, the equation for the unknown $z_h\in V_h$
$$a(z_h,v_h)=a(u,v_h)\qquad\text{for every }v_h\in V_h$$
is the **Ritz equation**; any solution $z_h$ is called a Ritz projection of
$u$. The item [[lem-parabolic-ritz-projection-well-defined]] proves that for
every $u$ there is exactly one solution, denoted $R_hu$, and that these
solutions define a bounded linear map $R_h:V\to V_h$. The form need not be
symmetric.

Let $\widehat V_j$ and $V_j$ be reference and physical spaces related by
invertible affine Piola maps $P_j:\widehat V_j\to V_j$. Let $\widehat D_j$
and $D_j$ be the corresponding differential operators, and assume the
proved affine identities $D_jP_j=P_{j+1}\widehat D_j$ from
[[thm-affine-piola-differential-and-trace-moment-identities]]. Suppose
reference interpolation operators $\widehat I_j$ are defined on spaces
containing the relevant inputs and satisfy
$$\widehat D_j\widehat I_j=\widehat I_{j+1}\widehat D_j$$
there. Define the physical interpolants by Piola conjugation
$I_j=P_j\widehat I_jP_j^{-1}$. Then
$$D_jI_j=I_{j+1}D_j$$
on every input for which these compositions are defined. This is conditional
on the reference commuting identity; it does not assert that arbitrary
unisolvent degrees of freedom commute.

Assume Countable Choice. For $u\in H^1(K)$, use the facet traces of
[[lem-crouzeix-raviart-simplex-traces-and-green-identity]] and define its local
face-average interpolant by
$$I_K^{CR}u:=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\left(\frac1{|F|}\int_Fu\,dS\right)\phi_{K,F},$$
where $\phi_{K,F}$ is the explicit polynomial in
[[def-crouzeix-raviart-local-p1-element]]. On a finite matching mesh, define
$I_h^{CR}u$ cellwise by $(I_h^{CR}u)|_K=I_K^{CR}(u|_K)$. For a global
$u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, the cell traces agree on interior facets and vanish on
boundary facets, so this formula has the intended global Crouzeix–Raviart
degrees of freedom. The local estimate item proves its fractional
approximation bounds.

current_use.excerpt:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ and $\mathcal T$ be as in
[[def-crouzeix-raviart-global-space]], let $V:=H^1_0(\Omega)$, let
$V_h:=V_h^{CR,0}$, and let $f\in L^2(\Omega)$. The exact Poisson form and
load are
$$a(u,v):=\int_\Omega\nabla u\cdot\nabla v\,dx,\qquad F(v):=\int_\Omega f v\,dx\quad (u,v\in V).$$
An exact solution is a $u\in V$ satisfying $a(u,v)=F(v)$ for every $v\in V$.
For $v_h,w_h\in V_h$, define the broken form and discrete load by
$$a_h(v_h,w_h):=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K\nabla v_h\cdot\nabla w_h\,dx, \qquad F_h(w_h):=\int_\Omega f w_h\,dx.$$
The discrete problem is to find $u_h\in V_h$ such that
$a_h(u_h,w_h)=F_h(w_h)$ for every $w_h\in V_h$.

Assume Countable Choice for the graph-space uniqueness and $L^2$ conventions of [[def-na-hcurl-space]]. Let $V_h=N_h^1$ be the lowest-order edge space on a finite tetrahedral mesh, as in [[def-na-lowest-order-whitney-de-rham-spaces]]. It is finite dimensional: restriction to the finitely many cells injects it into the finite product of the local spaces, each spanned by at most six Whitney edge fields. Injectivity holds because the cells cover $\Omega$ up to their measure-zero facets. Use the componentwise real $L^2$ inner product defined in [[def-na-hcurl-space]]. Define its curl kernel and the $L^2$ gauge space by
$$K_h:=\{v_h\in V_h:\operatorname{curl}v_h=0\},\qquad Z_h:=V_h\cap K_h^\perp.$$
The quotient $\dot V_h:=V_h/K_h$ has norm $\|[v_h]\|_{\operatorname{curl}}:=\|\operatorname{curl}v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$; this is well-defined and positive definite because two representatives differ by an element of $K_h$. The bilinear form induced by curl-curl is $a_h([u_h],[v_h])=(\operatorname{curl}u_h,\operatorname{curl}v_h)_{L^2}$. A representative of a quotient solution is fixed by the gauge condition $u_h\in Z_h$. The mixed gauge system uses a multiplier $p_h\in K_h$:
$$a_h(u_h,v_h)+(p_h,v_h)_{L^2}=f(v_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h),\qquad (u_h,q_h)_{L^2}=0\quad(q_h\in K_h).$$
The quotient energy norm, rather than the full $H(\operatorname{curl})$ norm, is the norm controlled by this definition.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine tetrahedral mesh. The four face-normal fluxes are unisolvent on each $RT_0(K)$, and matching face fluxes assemble a global $H(\operatorname{div})$ field. For smooth scalar $f$, smooth vector fields $u,v$, and the canonical interpolants determined by vertex values, oriented edge circulations, oriented face-normal fluxes, and cell integrals, the interpolation maps satisfy cellwise
$$
abla I_h^0f=I_h^1
abla f,\qquad \operatorname{curl}I_h^1u=I_h^2\operatorname{curl}u,\qquad \operatorname{div}I_h^2v=I_h^3\operatorname{div}v.$$
Any assignment of one real oriented value to each global mesh edge determines a unique assembled field in $N_h^1$; any assignment of one real oriented flux to each global mesh face determines a unique assembled field in $N_h^2$. These assemblies belong to $H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$ and $H(\operatorname{div};\Omega)$, respectively, with the global spaces and conventions of [[def-na-lowest-order-whitney-de-rham-spaces]]. Applying the local moment identities to polynomial cell restrictions also proves that the global finite-element spaces form the subcomplex $W_h^0\xrightarrow{
abla}N_h^1\xrightarrow{\operatorname{curl}}N_h^2\xrightarrow{\operatorname{div}}N_h^3$. The canonical interpolation identities themselves apply to smooth inputs; they do not extend the canonical edge moments to arbitrary $H(\operatorname{curl})$ inputs.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V_h,Q_h$ be the stable mini-element spaces on a bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral domain with a conforming mesh, with viscosity $\nu>0$, and let $Z_h=\{v_h:b(v_h,q_h)=0\ \forall q_h\in Q_h\}$. Choose bases of $V_h,Q_h$, let $M$ be the velocity mass matrix, $A$ the Stokes stiffness matrix, and $B$ the constraint matrix with entries $B_{\ell j}=b(\phi_j,\chi_\ell)$. The mass-orthogonal projector onto $Z_h$ is
$$P_M=I-M^{-1}B^T(BM^{-1}B^T)^{-1}B.$$
On the mean-zero pressure coordinates, both the mass pressure Schur matrix $BM^{-1}B^T$ and stiffness pressure Schur matrix $BA^{-1}B^T$ are positive definite. Before imposing the pressure gauge on the full continuous P1 space, the constant pressure is exactly the one-dimensional nullspace of $B^T$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded contractible Lipschitz polyhedron
with connected boundary, and let $X$ be the full-kernel orthogonal gauge of
[[def-na-pe11-maxwell-cavity-eigenproblem]]. Every sequence in $X$ bounded in
$H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$ has a subsequence converging strongly in
$L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$. Equivalently, the inclusion of $X$, with its
$H(\operatorname{curl})$ graph norm, into $L^2$ is compact. Moreover there
is a constant $C_\Omega$ such that
$$\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \qquad(u\in X).$$
Thus the curl form is coercive on $X$ in its $H(\operatorname{curl})$ graph
norm.

$$\operatorname{div}\Pi_hv=P_0\operatorname{div}v,\qquad \|\Pi_hv\|_{H(\operatorname{div})}\le C\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div})},$$
where $C$ depends on the domain and mesh shape bound, not mesh size. The construction uses the finite-dimensional $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto $Z_h$ and never applies facet moments to rough H(div)-only fields.

Assume Countable Choice, a bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral $D$ in dimension two or three, and a shape-regular conforming mesh. Let $C_I$ be the mesh-independent constant in the RT0 interpolation estimate and let $L$ be a coordinate-slab width for $D$. If $B_D$ is the actual right inverse of [[thm-na-bounded-lipschitz-domain-divergence-right-inverse]], define
$$S_hq_h:=I_hB_Dq_h,\qquad C_R:=C_I C_{\rm div}(L+\operatorname{diam}D).$$
Then $S_h:Q_h\to V_h$ is a linear right inverse of divergence and $\|S_hq_h\|_{L^2(D)}\le C_R\|q_h\|_{L^2(D)}$. Consequently $\|S_hq_h\|_{H(\operatorname{div})}\le\sqrt{1+C_R^2}\|q_h\|_2$. When $Q_h\ne\{0\}$, the RT0/P0 inf-sup constant satisfies $\beta_h\ge(1+C_R^2)^{-1/2}$ uniformly in mesh size.

Assume Countable Choice and the hypotheses of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]] and [[lem-nitsche-global-boundary-flux-bound]]. Put $C_\partial$ as in the latter item and let $\theta\in\{0,1\}$. If
$$\gamma_0>\frac{(1+\theta)^2C_\partial^2}{4},$$
then for every $v_h\in V_h$,
$$a_h^\theta(v_h,v_h)\ge\lambda_\theta\|v_h\|_{E,h}^2,\qquad \lambda_\theta:=\frac{1+\gamma_0-\sqrt{(1-\gamma_0)^2+(1+\theta)^2C_\partial^2}}{2}>0.$$
Thus the sufficient threshold is $C_\partial^2/4$ for the nonsymmetric form and $C_\partial^2$ for the symmetric form. These are thresholds certified by the displayed inverse-trace bound, not asserted to be necessary for each individual mesh.

Assume Countable Choice and the Poisson/Nitsche setup of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]] on a connected bounded polyhedral $\Omega$. Let $u\in H^{1+r}(\Omega)$, $r>1/2$, solve $-\Delta u=f\in L^2(\Omega)$ with Dirichlet trace $g$, and let $u_h^\theta$ solve the discrete problem for $\theta\in\{0,1\}$. Use the comparison seminorm $\|\cdot\|_{\#,h}$ of the definition. Put $C_\partial$ as in [[lem-nitsche-global-boundary-flux-bound]], and assume
$$\gamma_0>(1+\theta)^2C_\partial^2/4.$$
The discrete solution exists uniquely, and
$$\|u-u_h^\theta\|_{\#,h}\le C_\theta\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_{\#,h},\qquad C_\theta:=1+\frac{(2+\theta C_\partial+\gamma_0)(1+C_\partial^2)}{\lambda_\theta},$$
where $\lambda_\theta$ is the positive coercivity constant in [[lem-nitsche-penalty-coercivity]]. If, in addition, the Nitsche comparison-norm approximation bound [A2] holds with exponent $t>0$, then
$$\|u-u_h^\theta\|_{\#,h}\le C_\theta C_I\left(\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K^{2t}\|u\|_{H^{1+t}(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
The result keeps the weak Dirichlet trace unconstrained in $V_h$.

Assume Countable Choice and the nonsymmetric Nitsche setup of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]] and [[thm-nitsche-consistency-and-energy-quasioptimality]] with penalty above its coercivity threshold. Put $e:=u-u_h^0\in L^2(\Omega)$, and let $\zeta_e\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ solve $\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\nabla\zeta_e=\int_\Omega ve$ for all $v\in H^1_0(\Omega)$. Let $s\in(1/2,1]$ and assume the genuine dual regularity hypothesis [A1]. The proved comparison interpolation theorem supplies $z_h:=I_{h,0}\zeta_e\in Y_h$ with $\|\zeta_e-z_h\|_{\#,h}\le C_D h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|\zeta_e\|_{H^{1+s}}$, and the proved weighted flux trace theorem supplies
$$\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n\zeta_e\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C_T h^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2}\|\zeta_e\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)},\qquad 0<h\le\ell_\Omega:=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega).$$
Then
$$\|e\|_2\le\left(M_0C_DC_Rh^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}+C_TC_Rh^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2}\right)\|e\|_{\#,h},$$
where $M_0:=2+\gamma_0\ge1$ and $C_D,C_T$ are mesh-uniform for the fixed domain. Since $s>1/2$ and $h\le\ell_\Omega$, the right side is $O(h^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2})\|e\|_{\#,h}$ after absorbing the fixed constants. The surviving boundary term prevents claiming the symmetric $h^s$ factor from dual regularity alone.

Assume Countable Choice and the symmetric Nitsche setup of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]] and [[thm-nitsche-consistency-and-energy-quasioptimality]] with penalty above the symmetric coercivity threshold. Let $e:=u-u_h^1\in L^2(\Omega)$ and let $\zeta_e\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ solve the adjoint Poisson problem $\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\nabla\zeta_e\,dx=\int_\Omega ve\,dx$ for every $v\in H^1_0(\Omega)$. Assume its dual regularity bound [A1]
$$\|\zeta_e\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)}\le C_R\|e\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad s\in(1/2,1],$$
The proved interpolation theorem [[thm-nitsche-zero-boundary-fractional-comparison-interpolation]] supplies $z_h:=I_{h,0}\zeta_e\in Y_h$ and a mesh-uniform constant $C_D$ with
$$\|\zeta_e-z_h\|_{\#,h}\le C_D h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|\zeta_e\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)},\qquad 0<h\le\ell_\Omega:=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega).$$
Set $C_\partial$ as in [[lem-nitsche-global-boundary-flux-bound]] and preserve the original constant $M_1:=2+C_\partial+\gamma_0$. Then
$$\|u-u_h^1\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le M_1 C_D C_R h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|u-u_h^1\|_{\#,h},$$
where the all-comparison-space symmetric form bound with this same $M_1$ is proved below. The dual elliptic regularity estimate remains an explicit PDE hypothesis. If, in addition, the general higher-order/local primal energy approximation hypothesis [A3] holds with exponent $t>0$, then
$$\|u-u_h^1\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le M_1 C_D C_R C_\theta C_I h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\left(\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K^{2t}\|u\|_{H^{1+t}(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
The primal branch retains its full exponent range and local broken-norm hypothesis; the zero-boundary P1 interpolation theorem supplies the dual approximation and does not replace that branch.

Let $d\ge1$. If $d=1$, let the cells be a finite oriented interval mesh from [[def-pe04-one-dimensional-interval-mesh-and-broken-polynomials]]; if $d\ge2$, let them form a finite matching affine simplicial mesh. On every cell assume diagonal-norm SBP data of [[def-pe04-diagonal-norm-sbp-element-data]], with paired interior face nodes, equal paired weights, and opposite outward normals. Let $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$ be constant, and let the differentiable nodal state $U_K(t)$ solve the upwind SBP-SAT method of [[def-pe04-upwind-sbp-sat-transport-discretization]] with prescribed inflow values $g_{F,q}$ where $b_{K,F}:=\beta\cdot n_{K,F}<0$. Write $\omega_{F,q}$ for the diagonal entries of the face norm. On an interior face oriented from $K^-$ to $K^+$, set $b_F=\beta\cdot n_F$ and $[U]_{F,q}=U^+_{F,q}-U^-_{F,q}$. Let $\Gamma_+$ and $\Gamma_-$ denote the boundary faces with positive and negative outward speed, respectively. For $d=1$, each face has one endpoint node and its face sum is a one-point sum. The discrete energy $E_h=\frac12\sum_K U_K^TH_KU_K$ satisfies
$$\frac{dE_h}{dt}+\frac12\sum_{F\text{ interior}}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}|b_F|[U]_{F,q}^2+\frac12\sum_{F\subset\Gamma_+}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}b_{K,F}U_{F,q}^2+\frac12\sum_{F\subset\Gamma_-}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}|b_{K,F}|(U_{F,q}-g_{F,q})^2=\frac12\sum_{F\subset\Gamma_-}\sum_q\omega_{F,q}|b_{K,F}|g_{F,q}^2.$$
Consequently, zero inflow data give a nonincreasing SBP norm.

$$\mathcal P_K(u)=\left\{p\in\mathbb P_p(K):\int_K(u-p)w\,d\mu=0\text{ for every }w\in\mathbb P_p(K)\right\}.$$

On each fixed contact mesh in [[def-signorini-dual-mortar-contact-pair]], assume $K_h\subseteq K$, the elasticity form is bounded and coercive on $V_h$ with constants $M,\alpha>0$, and $F$ is bounded. Then the nodal contact variational inequality has a unique displacement $u_h$ and a unique multiplier $\lambda_h=\sum_i\lambda_i\chi_i\in\Lambda_h^+$ satisfying
$$a(u_h,v_h)-F(v_h)=b_h(v_h,\lambda_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h),$$
$$g_i:=u_h(a_i)\cdot n-I_h\psi(a_i)\ge0,\quad \lambda_i\ge0,\quad \lambda_i g_i=0\quad(0\le i\le N).$$
These saddle equations are equivalent to the discrete VI, and the integrated complementarity residual is exactly $\mathcal R_h:=\int_{\Gamma_C}\lambda_h(T_Cu_h\cdot n-I_h\psi)\,ds=\sum_i d_i\lambda_i g_i=0$. The trace-pair inf-sup bound is at least $1/\sqrt3$ in the stated $L^2$ norms by [[lem-signorini-dual-mortar-biorthogonality-and-infsup]], and the displacement satisfies $\|u_h\|_V\le\|F\|_{V^*}/\alpha$. The coupling uses exact edge integrals and has no contact quadrature defect.

Assume Countable Choice, and let $u\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$ solve the stated strong problem. For every continuous, zero-boundary function $w$ whose restriction to each cell has square-integrable values and square-integrable weak first derivatives, define
$$\|w\|_{\mathrm{SD},h}^2:=\epsilon\|\nabla w\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2+\omega\|w\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2+\sum_K\delta_K\|b\cdot\nabla w\|_{L^2(K)}^2.$$
$$M_2:=|\Omega|^{1/2}\|D^2u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},\quad B:=\|b\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},\quad C:=\|c\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},\quad \delta_*:=\max_K\delta_K.$$
Then the discrete form is coercive:
$$a_h(v_h,v_h)\ge\frac34\|v_h\|_{\mathrm{SD},h}^2\qquad(v_h\in V_h),$$
the discrete problem has a unique solution $u_h$, and the method is consistent, $a_h(u,v_h)=F_h(v_h)$. Moreover, with $C_*$ depending only on dimension, shape regularity, and the interpolation constant,
$$\|u-u_h\|_{\mathrm{SD},h}\le C_*M_2\left[\left(\sqrt{\epsilon}+\frac{B}{\sqrt{\omega}}\right)h+\left(\sqrt{\omega}+\frac{C}{\sqrt{\omega}}\right)h^2+B\sqrt{\delta_*}\,h+\sqrt{\delta_*}\left(\sqrt d\,\epsilon+Bh+Ch^2\right)\right].$$
This is a P1 estimate for the stated strong regularity and parameter branch; it does not claim stability for unrestricted multidimensional parameters or weaker regularity.

current_use.excerpt:
Assume Countable Choice and the setup of [[def-crouzeix-raviart-face-average-interpolant]], a
shape-regular affine mesh, and $1/2<r\le1$. The face-average interpolant is
defined for every $u\in H^{1+r}(K)$ by the traces of
[[lem-crouzeix-raviart-simplex-traces-and-green-identity]] and reproduces
$\mathbb P_1(K)$. Uniformly over all cells,
$$\|\nabla(u-I_K^{CR}u)\|_{L^2(K)} \le C h_K^r|u|_{H^{1+r}(K)},\qquad \|u-I_K^{CR}u\|_{L^2(K)} \le C h_K^{1+r}|u|_{H^{1+r}(K)}.$$
For each facet $F\subset\partial K$,
$$h_F^{-1/2}\|\gamma_F(u-I_K^{CR}u)\|_{L^2(F)} \le C h_K^r|u|_{H^{1+r}(K)}.$$
If $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, then the global interpolant has matching interior
face means and zero boundary face means, so $I_h^{CR}u\in V_h^{CR,0}$.

historical_HEAD_use.excerpt: Assume Countable Choice. Let $U_h$ be a finite-dimensional cellwise-constant control space with nonempty box $Q_h$, and restrict the exact reduced objective $\widehat J$ of [[def-linear-elliptic-pde-constrained-control-problem]] to $Q_h$. Let $q_h^*$ be its minimizer and let $L_h\ge\|S|_{U_h}\|^2+\alpha$, where $S$ is the linear part of the continuous state-to-observation map and $\alpha>0$. Assume the residual- and projection-evaluation routines satisfy the finite-return admissibility conditions in [[alg-fem-control-proximal-gradient-certified-residual]]. Then that finite-budget algorithm terminates in finite time after at most $N$ iterations and at most $N$ calls to each routine, returning \texttt{inconclusive}, \texttt{budget-exhausted}, or \texttt{certified}. Every \texttt{certified} return at $q\in Q_h$ with reported bound $\rho=\tilde\rho+\delta/L_h$ satisfies $\|q-P_{Q_h}(q-\nabla\widehat J(q)/L_h)\|_U\le\rho\le\tau$, and consequently $\|q-q_h^*\|_U\le(L_h/\alpha)\rho=(L_h/\alpha)\tilde\rho+\delta/\alpha$. This bounds distance to the control-mesh minimizer of the exact PDE objective; it is not an error estimate between that minimizer and the unrestricted PDE optimum.

current_use.excerpt:
Assume Countable Choice. Use either mesh branch and the nodal space defined
in [[lem-pe12-quasiuniform-mass-inverse-decay]]. For $d\ge2$, assume
$\Omega$ is a bounded polyhedral open set whose boundary is locally a graph
of a Lipschitz function with $\Omega$ on one side; for $d=1$, use a bounded
nonempty interval or a finite nonempty union of bounded intervals with
pairwise disjoint closures. Let $1\le p<\infty$. There is a linear map
$$
Q_h:W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)\longrightarrow V_h
$$
with the following construction. Fix a nonnegative $\rho\in C_c^\infty(B(0,1))$
with $\int\rho=1$, let $E_0$ be extension by zero, and set
$S_hv=\rho_h*E_0v$ with $\rho_h(x)=h^{-d}\rho(x/h)$. The degree-$k$
coefficient of $Q_hv$ at every interior node $z$ is $S_hv(z)$; every
boundary-node coefficient is zero. For all sufficiently fine meshes,
$$\|v-Q_hv\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le Ch\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad \|\nabla Q_hv\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}.$$
Consequently $Q_hv\to v$ in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ for each
$v\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$. Constants are uniform over the fixed mesh family
and may depend on $d,k,p,\Omega,\theta,\sigma$ and $\rho$. The operator
$Q_h$ is not asserted to be a projector.

current_use.excerpt:
Assume Countable Choice and fix a degree $k\ge1$. Take a sequence of meshes
with $h\to0$ in either branch and use the
zero-boundary Lagrange spaces $V_h$ from
[[lem-pe12-quasiuniform-mass-inverse-decay]]: globally quasi-uniform,
shape-regular matching affine simplices on a bounded Lipschitz polyhedral
open set in $d\ge2$ (with the local graph-chart convention of
[[lem-pe12-boundary-preserving-quasi-interpolation]]), or interval
partitions of a nonempty bounded interval (or a finite nonempty union of
intervals with disjoint closures) in $d=1$. For $f\in L^1(\Omega)$ define
$P_hf\in V_h$ by the finite mass system
$$
\int_\Omega (P_hf)w_h=\int_\Omega fw_h\qquad(w_h\in V_h).
$$
This is well-defined, agrees on $L^2(\Omega)$ with the $L^2$-orthogonal
projection, and is the identity on $V_h$. There are constants independent
of $h$ such that
$$\|P_hf\|_{L^r(\Omega)}\le C_r\|f\|_{L^r(\Omega)}\qquad(1\le r\le\infty).$$
For every $1<p<\infty$ and $v\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$,
$$\|\nabla P_hv\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C_p\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad P_hv\longrightarrow v\quad\text{in }W^{1,p}(\Omega).$$
For the PE12 application, additionally assume the Axiom of Choice and
$p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. The compact embedding
[[lem-pe12-w1p-compact-l2-embedding]] makes $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$ a dense
subspace of $H=L^2(\Omega)$, and
[[lem-pe12-w0p-separable-reflexive]] supplies the separable reflexive Banach
structure. Thus these spaces form the evolution triple of
[[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]] and
[[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]], and the $P_h$ above is its $H$-orthogonal
projector. Together with any time partitions whose maximum step tends to
zero it satisfies the projector clauses in
[[def-pe12-stable-conforming-fem-family]]. For every $d\ge2$, the uniform
Kuhn/Freudenthal meshes of $\Omega=(0,1)^d$, and for $d=1$ the uniform
interval meshes of $\Omega=(0,1)$, are explicit nonempty instances throughout
that full strict $p$ range. Time refinement is independent of spatial
refinement.

current_use.excerpt:
Let $\Omega=\{(x,y,z):(\sqrt{x^2+y^2}-R)^2+z^2<r^2\}$ be a solid torus with $R>r>0$. Define
$$u(x,y,z)=\left(-\frac{y}{x^2+y^2},\frac{x}{x^2+y^2},0\right).$$
This is a smooth curl-free and divergence-free field on $\overline\Omega$, tangent to the boundary, whose circulation around the core circle is $2\pi$. Here “harmonic” means curl and divergence both vanish with zero normal boundary component. It is a concrete nonzero-period field caused by the handle; the nonzero period proves it is not the gradient of a single-valued $C^1$ potential. It is the continuous model for the nontrivial cohomology components described in [[thm-na-lowest-order-discrete-de-rham-cohomology-and-harmonic-modes]].

Assume Countable Choice and the bounded polyhedral mesh setting, spaces,
form and data of [[thm-parabolic-fem-semidiscrete-existence-energy]]. Let $u$
be the continuous solution supplied by
[[thm-parabolic-variational-wellposedness-and-energy-stability]] on the same
evolution triple and let $u_h$ be the corresponding semidiscrete solution.
For this error identity, assume the additional regularity $u\in H^1(0,T;V)$,
meaning $u,u'\in L^2(0,T;V)$ with the unique continuous representative
supplied by [[lem-parabolic-projection-time-product-rule]]. Let
$P_h:V\to V_h$ be a fixed bounded linear
comparison map, define
$$\rho(t)=P_hu(t)-u(t),\qquad\theta(t)=u_h(t)-P_hu(t),$$
and let $\mathcal R_h(t)\in V_h^*$ be the full residual
$$\mathcal R_h(t)(v_h)=(\rho'(t),v_h)_H+a(t;\rho(t),v_h).$$
Then for almost every $t$ and every $v_h\in V_h$,
$$(\theta'(t),v_h)_H+a(t;\theta(t),v_h)=-\mathcal R_h(t)(v_h),$$
and for every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\|\theta(t)\|_H^2+\alpha\int_0^t\|\theta(s)\|_V^2ds \le\|\theta(0)\|_H^2+ \alpha^{-1}\int_0^t\|\mathcal R_h(s)\|_{V_h^*}^2ds.$$

Assume Countable Choice for the graph spaces and real $L^2$ product as in [[def-na-curl-curl-kernel-quotient-gauge]]. Let $V_h$ be that finite-dimensional real edge space, $K_h=\ker(\operatorname{curl}|_{V_h})$, and $Z_h=V_h\cap K_h^\perp$. Here $V_h^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(V_h,\mathbb R)$ is the algebraic dual of [[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]. For every $f\in V_h^*$ there is a unique pair $(u_h,p_h)\in Z_h\times K_h$ satisfying
$$ (\operatorname{curl}u_h,\operatorname{curl}v_h)_{L^2}+(p_h,v_h)_{L^2}=f(v_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h),\qquad (u_h,q_h)_{L^2}=0\quad(q_h\in K_h).$$
The gauge multiplier is the $L^2$ Riesz representative of $f|_{K_h}$. The quotient solution satisfies the exact stability identity
$$\|\operatorname{curl}u_h\|_{L^2}=\|f|_{Z_h}\|_{(Z_h,\|\operatorname{curl}(\cdot)\|_{L^2})^*},\qquad \|p_h\|_{L^2}=\|f|_{K_h}\|_{(K_h,\|\cdot\|_{L^2})^*}.$$
The constraint form $b(v,q)=(v,q)_{L^2}$ has inf-sup constant one when $K_h\ne\{0\}$, $V_h$ has the $H(\operatorname{curl})$ graph norm and $K_h$ has the $L^2$ norm; if $K_h=\{0\}$ the constraint is vacuous. The curl form is coercive with constant one on $Z_h$ in the quotient curl norm. No mesh-uniform estimate in the full graph norm is claimed here.

Assume Countable Choice and the real form and spaces of [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]] on a finite conforming triangular mesh. For every admissible local input to [[alg-na-practical-dpg-finite-riesz-solves]], the exact factorization terminates after $O(N_K^3)$ scalar arithmetic operations once its Gram entries and right-hand side are formed; it returns `singular-test-matrix` exactly for a dependent input family, and on an independent family it returns the unique finite Riesz representative. Let $U_h\subset U$ consist of volume fields $\sigma_h|_K\in P_1(K)^2$, $u_h|_K\in P_1(K)$, continuous scalar traces $\widehat u_h|_{\partial K}\in\widetilde P_2(\partial K)$, and conservative normal traces $\widehat\sigma_{n,h}|_{\partial K}\in P_1(\partial K)$. This is finite-dimensional. Let $V_r=\prod_K(P_3(K)^2\times P_3(K))$, presented cellwise by fixed ordered bases, and let $T_r:U_h\to V_r$ be the assembled finite Riesz map. On each fixed basis the unique local Riesz representatives assemble to a bounded linear map satisfying $\|T_rw_h\|_V\le\|b\|\|w_h\|_U$. Now assume the continuous primal and adjoint graph inf-sup constants have minimum $\beta>0$. Let $\Pi:V\to V_r$ be the bounded Fortin map of [[lem-na-practical-dpg-fortin-p1-r3]], with $b(U_h,(I-\Pi)V)=0$ and $\|\Pi\|\le C_\Pi$. Then for every bounded load $F\in V'$, the practical DPG system tested with $T_r(U_h)$ has a unique solution $x_h$, and
$$\|x-x_h\|_U\le(1+\|b\|C_\Pi/\beta)\inf_{z_h\in U_h}\|x-z_h\|_U,$$
where $x$ is the exact continuous solution.

Its complementarity form is $Ag-f=\rho$, $g_i\ge0$, $\rho_i\ge0$, and $\rho_i g_i=0$. The scaling $\rho_i=d_i\lambda_i$ matches [[thm-signorini-mortar-contact-kkt-and-complementarity]], where $d_i>0$ is the diagonal dual-pair weight and $\lambda_i$ is the multiplier coefficient. For $f^{(1)}=(1,1/5)^T$, both gaps are positive and no constraint is active. For $f^{(2)}=(1,-1)^T$, the second constraint alone is active, with $g=(1/2,0)^T$ and $\rho=(0,1/2)^T$. This is an algebraic reduced model; the chosen matrix is not asserted to arise from a particular geometric mesh.

current_use.excerpt: [F92] Under the already assumed AC, every bounded Lipschitz domain $B$ has a bounded $H^1$ extension $E_B$ to $\mathbb R^3$, including graph-chart pieces and bounded annuli. For $v\in H^1(B)$, multiply $E_Bv$ by a fixed smooth cutoff equal to one near $\overline B$ and convolve with a unit-mass smooth approximate identity. The weak product rule and derivative commutation give $D^\alpha(\rho_\epsilon*(\zeta E_Bv))=\rho_\epsilon*D^\alpha(\zeta E_Bv)$ for $|\alpha|\le1$; approximate-identity convergence in $L^2$ for each of these four functions gives convergence in $H^1(B)$. Thus restrictions of ambient smooth functions are dense in $H^1(B)$, with the convergence of every weak derivative supplied rather than inferred from pointwise smoothing. The same argument on a bounded flat half-box or its even reflection supplies the flat-chart approximation. ([[lem-na-lipschitz-scalar-h1-h2-extension]], [[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]], [[prop-mollifier-families-are-l-one-approximate-identities]], [[thm-l-one-approximate-identities-converge-in-l-p]], [[thm-convolution-with-a-mollifier-is-smooth-and-differentiates-under-the-integral-sign]])

There are a subsequence, still indexed by $k$, and a unique
$u\in L^p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)\cap C([0,T];H)$ such that
$$\overline U_k\to u\quad\text{strongly in }L^r(0,T;H) \text{ for every }1\le r<\infty,\qquad \overline U_k\rightharpoonup u\text{ in }L^p(0,T;V),$$
the fluxes $a(x,\nabla\overline U_k)$ converge weakly in
$L^{p'}((0,T)\times\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ to $a(x,\nabla u)$, and
$$u'+A(u)=f\quad\text{in }L^{p'}(0,T;V^*),\qquad u(0)=u_0.$$
Existence of each discrete solution and uniform energy bounds are included
in [[thm-pe12-backward-euler-galerkin-existence-energy]]. The abstract
convergence claim is conditional on the FEM projector clauses. For
$\Omega=(0,1)$ in $d=1$ and $\Omega=(0,1)^d$ in each $d\ge2$, the explicit
fixed-degree interval and Kuhn/Freudenthal simplex families of
[[thm-pe12-l2-projector-w1p-stability]] verify those clauses for any
independent time partitions with vanishing maximum step. These are concrete
nonempty instances of the theorem on the full approved strict $p$ range.

current_use.excerpt:
Assume Countable Choice and the differentiable continuous state/adjoint setting of [[thm-parabolic-adjoint-gradient-sensitivity]]. Let $u,p$ and $u_h,p_h$ denote the continuous and semidiscrete state/adjoint pairs. Write
$$r[\eta]=D_\theta\phi(u(T),\theta)[\eta]+\int_0^T D_\theta L(t,u(t),\theta)[\eta]dt,\qquad r_h[\eta]=D_\theta\phi_h(u_h(T),\theta)[\eta]+\int_0^T D_\theta L_h(t,u_h(t),\theta)[\eta]dt.$$
Assume their gradients $g,g_h\in(\mathbb R^m)^*$ have the representations, for every $\eta\in\mathbb R^m$,
$$g[\eta]=r[\eta]+(p(0),D_\theta u_0[\eta])_H+\int_0^T\bigl(\langle D_\theta f[\eta],p\rangle-D_\theta a[\eta](u,p)\bigr)dt,$$
$$g_h[\eta]=r_h[\eta]+(p_h(0),D_\theta u_{0,h}[\eta])_H+\int_0^T\bigl(\langle D_\theta f_h[\eta],p_h\rangle-D_\theta a_h[\eta](u_h,p_h)\bigr)dt.$$
The continuous representation is supplied by the cited adjoint theorem; the semidiscrete representation is an explicit hypothesis here. Assume $u,p\in H^1(0,T;V)$, the parabolic form and its parameter derivative are uniformly bounded, and the form is coercive with constant $\alpha>0$. Suppose the forward state and time-reversed adjoint both satisfy the hypotheses of [[thm-parabolic-semidiscrete-ritz-error-splitting-and-energy-bound]], with operator-norm $C^1$ comparison maps $P_{u,h}(t),P_{p,h}(t):V\to V_h$. For the state comparison map, set $\rho_u=P_{u,h}u-u$, $\vartheta_u=u_h-P_{u,h}u$, and
$$\mathcal R_u(t)(v_h)=(\rho_u'(t),v_h)_H+a_\theta(t;\rho_u(t),v_h),\qquad \rho_u'=P_{u,h}'(t)u+P_{u,h}(t)u'-u'.$$
In reverse time $s=T-t$, put $q(s)=p(T-s)$ and $\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)=P_{p,h}(T-s)$; define $\rho_p(s)=\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)-q(s)$, $\vartheta_p(s)=p_h(T-s)-\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)$, and $\mathcal R_p(s)(v_h)=(\rho_p'(s),v_h)_H+a_\theta(T-s;v_h,\rho_p(s))$. The projection product rule gives $\rho_p'=\widetilde P_{p,h}'q+\widetilde P_{p,h}q'-q'$, with $\widetilde P_{p,h}'(s)=-P_{p,h}'(T-s)$. The Ritz supplier gives, for $z=u,p$,
$$\|z-z_h\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}\le E_z:=\|\rho_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}+\alpha^{-1/2}\left(\|\vartheta_z(0)\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|\mathcal R_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2\right)^{1/2},$$
where the adjoint's initial trace means its terminal trace in original time. In particular, $\mathcal R_z$ contains the derivative of the time-dependent projection; it cannot be dropped from this hypothesis.

current_use.excerpt:
On arbitrary time partitions with maximum step $\delta_h\to0$, every selection of step solutions satisfies, uniformly in $h$,
$$\max_n\|\Pi_hU_h^n\|_2^2+\sum_n\|\Pi_h(U_h^n-U_h^{n-1})\|_2^2+\sum_n\tau_n B_{h,p}(U_h^n)^p\le C.$$
Here $B_{h,p},D_{h,p},S_{h,p},G_h$ are as in [[lem-fv-conforming-companion-and-test-recovery]]. Extend $\overline U_h$ by $U_h^n$ on $(t_{n-1},t_n]$. The piecewise affine interpolation of $\Pi_hU_h^n$ has derivative bounded in $L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$. There are a subsequence and $u\in L^p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ such that
$$\Pi_h\overline U_h\to u\text{ in }L^r(0,T;H)\ (1\le r<\infty)\text{ and in }L^p(Q),$$
$$E_h\overline U_h\rightharpoonup u\text{ in }L^p(0,T;V),\qquad G_h\overline U_h\rightharpoonup\nabla u\text{ in }L^p(Q;\mathbb R^d).$$
No mesh/time coupling or time-step ratio restriction is required.

current_use.excerpt: The condition-number theorem concerns the ideal exact local and coarse solves and the spectrum of the preconditioned interface operators. It does not bound elapsed time, communication, memory, or total arithmetic work. For example, under a dense direct-solver model with coarse dimension $n_c$, a coarse factorization uses $O(n_c^3)$ arithmetic and $O(n_c^2)$ storage, while a dense local factorization for subdomain dimensions $n_i$ uses $O(\sum_i n_i^3)$ arithmetic before parallel scheduling. Therefore a growing primal space can make the coarse solve dominate even while the condition number remains polylogarithmic. An inexact local or coarse solve requires its own spectral-equivalence and cost hypotheses.

Let $\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be the completion of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ in the norm $\|u\|_{\dot H^1}=\|
abla u\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$, using its $L^6$ representative and the trace from [[lem-bem-lipschitz-trace-and-lifting]]. For $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$, consider the equation for $u\in\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)$
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}
abla u\cdot
abla v\,dx=\langle\lambda,\gamma vangle_\Gamma\qquad(v\in\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)).$$
Call such a function a weak single-layer potential and write $S\lambda=u$ when it exists. Define the exterior energy space $E^+(\Omega^+)=\{u\in H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega^+):u\in L^6(\Omega^+),\ 
abla u\in L^2(\Omega^+)\}$. For a weakly harmonic function $u^-\in H^1(\Omega^-)$, define its weak outward conormal by $\langle\partial_n^-u^-,gangle=\int_{\Omega^-}
abla u^-\cdot
abla L^-g$, where $L^-g$ is any $H^1$ trace lift. For a harmonic $u^+\in E^+(\Omega^+)$, use the same fixed normal $n$ by $\langle\partial_n^+u^+,gangle=-\int_{\Omega^+}
abla u^+\cdot
abla L^+g$ for a compactly supported local lift. In either case the value is independent of the lift: the difference of two lifts has zero trace, and weak harmonicity makes its gradient pairing zero. The exterior formula also gives $\int_{\Omega^+}
abla u^+\cdot
abla v^+=-\langle\partial_n^+u^+,\gamma^+v^+angle$ for every $v^+\in E^+(\Omega^+)$. Indeed, subtract a compactly supported lift of $\gamma^+v^+$; the remaining zero-trace finite-energy function is approximated in gradient norm by compactly supported zero-trace functions using radial cutoffs: $\|v^+
abla\chi_R\|_2\le C\|v^+\|_{L^6(\{R<|x|<2R\})}	o0$. Boundary-chart flattening, zero extension, inward translation, and convolution approximate each zero-trace cutoff by interior smooth tests, so weak harmonicity makes its gradient pairing zero. This proves the energy identity without a flux assumption at infinity. Existence, uniqueness, agreement with the displayed kernel for smooth densities, and the conormal jump are proved in [[thm-bem-single-layer-transmission-mapping-and-coercivity]]. The weak definition fixes the normalization at infinity through $u\in L^6(\mathbb R^3)$; arbitrary additive constants are excluded.

For $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ define the Laplace Calderon boundary operators by
$$V\lambda=\gamma S\lambda,\qquad K\phi=\tfrac12(\gamma^-D\phi+\gamma^+D\phi),$$
$$K'\lambda=\tfrac12(\partial_n^-S\lambda+\partial_n^+S\lambda),\qquad W\phi=-\partial_n^-D\phi=-\partial_n^+D\phi.$$
Here $\gamma S\lambda$ is the common trace, conormal traces use the orientation of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], and the last equality is meaningful because the weak double layer has a common conormal derivative. This page uses the real duality pairing between $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$. The well-definedness and bounded mapping properties of $V,K,K',W$ are proved in [[thm-bem-calderon-mapping-and-jump-identities]].
